findings.title: Create error path records legacy metric instead of storage metric
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Create when Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) with startStorage. No storage call succeeded and no legacy call was made, so the storage failure is recorded under the legacy histogram and the storage histogram misses the failure. The same copy-paste error is in Update at line 129. This corrupts mode/kind/method duration metrics and hides storage errors.

findings.title: Delete success records storage duration with object name as kind
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Delete the success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) passing the object name where every other call passes options.Kind. The kind label will get unbounded high-cardinality values (one per object name) and dashboards/alerts grouped by kind will be wrong for mode 3 deletes.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy completion recorded as storage duration
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection the background goroutine finishes a Legacy.DeleteCollection call but reports it with d.recordStorageDuration(... startLegacy). It should be d.recordLegacyDuration like Create/Delete/Update do. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors will appear under the storage metric and legacy metric will miss them.

findings.title: Async legacy write derives timeout context from request context
findings.body: Create (line 51), Delete (line 110), Update (line 135) and DeleteCollection (line 163) do go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) ; d.Legacy.*(ctx, ...) } capturing the incoming request ctx. When the API request finishes the request context is cancelled, so the fire-and-forget legacy write can be cancelled before it runs, defeating the mode-3 goal of keeping legacy as a safety copy. An async write must use a detached context such as context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or context.Background() with timeout, not the live request context.

findings.title: Async legacy writes silently drop errors and use stale object
findings.body: Create passes the original obj to Legacy.Create in the background goroutine instead of the created object returned by Storage, so server-assigned defaults/resourceVersion are not propagated to legacy and stores diverge. More generally all four write paths (Create line 55, Delete line 112, Update line 139, DeleteCollection line 165) discard the legacy error with only a metrics counter and no log, so legacy/unified drift in mode 3 is invisible. At minimum log the legacy failure with the object identity.

findings.title: Delete installs wrong logger in context
findings.body: Delete builds log with name/kind/method but then does ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of klog.NewContext(ctx, log) as Create/Update/List do. The per-request fields are dropped from the context logger, so subsequent storage/legacy log calls lose the name/kind context.
